players.product: laser annealing & wet-processing systems for leading-edge nodes

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 revenue came in at $165 million (flat from the prior quarter, at the midpoint of guidance) with EPS of $0.24; semiconductor was 67% of Q4 revenue, compound semiconductor $20 million, data storage $10 million. Q4 non-GAAP gross margin was 38%, as product mix moved toward lower-margin advanced packaging plus evaluation-system signoff effects. Full year 2025 revenue was $664 million (down 7%) with EPS of $1.33; the semiconductor business had a record year at $477 million, 72% of revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue $165 million, EPS $0.24, gross margin 38%; FY2025 revenue $664 million, EPS $1.33; semiconductor $477 million (72%)

quarterly_data.signal: Non-GAAP outlook: Q1 2026 revenue between $150 million and $170 million, gross margin between 37% and 38%, diluted EPS between $0.14 and $0.24. Full year 2026 revenue between $740 million and $800 million (midpoint $770 million, up 16%), gross margin between 41% and 43%, EPS between $1.50 and $1.85, with growth weighted to the second half on orders secured in H2 2025. The CFO expects gross margin to reach the 45% gross margin target in the second half of 2026 on higher-margin new products, data storage growth and higher volumes; tariffs ran about 100 basis points of gross margin headwind, with a slightly higher tariff regime baked into 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 revenue $150 million to $170 million; FY2026 revenue $740 million to $800 million (midpoint $770 million, up 16%); FY2026 EPS $1.50 to $1.85; 45% gross margin target in H2 2026

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 segment outlook from the CFO: semiconductor growth around 15% at the guide midpoint to about $550 million, driven by Tier 1 customers on AI and high-performance computing and more than offsetting declines in mature-node China business; compound semiconductor up about 1/3 to about $80 million; data storage to double to about $80 million; scientific and other down about 33% to about $60 million as large quantum computing orders do not repeat. Order backlog ended 2025 at $555 million, up $145 million (35% growth), reflecting strong order acceleration in H2 2025 that positions revenue growth principally in H2 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026: semiconductor about $550 million (~15% growth); compound semi about $80 million; data storage about $80 million; backlog $555 million (+$145 million, 35% growth)

quarterly_data.signal: Advanced packaging doubled from $75 million in 2024 to $150 million in 2025, driven by AI-related demand; Veeco won multiple orders for advanced wet processing and lithography systems from leading foundries, with strong demand from heterogeneous integration and 3D packaging, and met customers' extreme high-volume manufacturing ramp of advanced packaging for AI. The advanced packaging SAM for wet processing and lithography tools is projected to reach $650 million by 2029.
quarterly_data.figure: Advanced packaging $75 million (2024) to $150 million (2025); SAM $650 million by 2029

quarterly_data.signal: Memory penetration: Veeco is production tool of record at a leading HBM DRAM customer and recently shipped an LSA evaluation system to a second DRAM manufacturer; 2 IBD300 systems are under evaluation at leading DRAM customers with evaluations extended into 2026 (low-resistance films for advanced DRAM structures such as bitline, pitched as the fourth deposition technology for front-end semiconductor). Management cites the transition to HBM, stacked architectures and low-resistance metallization as driving new thermal processing and material requirements, and sees wet processing growth as customers scale capacity driven by AI and HBM.
quarterly_data.figure: LSA tool of record at a leading HBM DRAM customer; LSA evaluation at a second DRAM maker; 2 IBD300 evaluations extended into 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Logic/foundry annealing: LSA is production tool of record at all 3 Tier 1 logic customers; the next-generation NSA (nanosecond annealing) system has 2 evaluations at Tier 1 logic customers, an evaluation system is planned to ship to the third in 2026, and 2 evaluation sign-offs are expected during 2026 with potential pilot line orders shortly after (low thermal budget uses such as contact annealing and 3D device stacking). Annealing SAM is projected at $1.3 billion by 2029 as devices shrink and shallower, more precise anneals are required, and the IBD300 low-resistance metals platform plus ion beam EUV mask blank and pellicle deposition SAM at $500 million by 2029; management expects the semiconductor SAM to expand on investment in gate-all-around, high-bandwidth memory and 3D packaging, with IBD a key enabler of high-NA EUV adoption. In 2026 logic, foundry and memory customers are all increasing capacity for annealing tools.
quarterly_data.figure: LSA tool of record at all 3 Tier 1 logic customers; NSA 2 evaluations; annealing SAM $1.3 billion by 2029; ion beam SAM $500 million by 2029

quarterly_data.signal: Compound semiconductor new products: orders received for the new Propel 300-millimeter GaN-on-silicon system (GaN power and microLED) and the Lumina plus arsenide phosphide system (photonics and solar), driving revenue in H2 2026, with orders being taken for delivery into 2027. A pilot line order from a leading power IDM ships in 2026 and should drive incremental business approaching $15 million, with possible H2 2026 orders for 2027 shipment if the customer continues to ramp; a 300-millimeter Propel GaN-on-silicon tool for microLED is also in backlog.
quarterly_data.figure: Propel GaN-on-silicon pilot line order approaching $15 million (2026 shipment)

quarterly_data.signal: Data storage: customers are adopting Heat-Assisted Magnetic Recording (HAMR), raising capital intensity and CapEx; Veeco is fully booked for system orders for 2026 and has started booking orders into 2027. The first round of orders shipping in 2026 is for front-end fabs, and new orders are now arriving for back-end slider fabs for shipment in 2027 - a function of the number of heads shipping - giving 'legs into '27 and potentially beyond.'
quarterly_data.figure: Data storage fully booked for 2026; slider fab orders for 2027 shipment

quarterly_data.signal: China: 2 LSA tool shipments to customers in China that were under customs review were resolved and $15 million of revenue on those systems was recognized in Q4 2025. China was 27% of 2025 revenue, down on lower laser annealing system sales, and 23% of Q4 revenue; Asia Pacific was 54% of Q4 revenue, mainly Taiwan semiconductor sales. On the Axcelis merger, shareholders of both companies approved it on February 6, regulatory approvals are secured in several key jurisdictions, clearance in China is still pending, and closing is anticipated in the second half of 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: $15 million China LSA revenue recognized in Q4; China 27% of 2025 revenue; Axcelis close expected H2 2026
